title: User interview: invoice approval delays
purpose: Understand where invoice approvals stall at a mid-size logistics firm
objectives: How long do invoice approvals take end to end?
Who can approve invoices above the limit?
What workaround do teams use today?

brief.text: Interviewee: Dana Okafor, accounts payable lead at Harbor Freight Partners (fictional). Hypothesis: approvals stall when the second approver is away. Avoid pitching any product.

turns.text: Thanks for making time, Dana. How long does an invoice usually take from arrival to approval?
Honestly it's quick, about a day for most invoices.
Anything under five thousand euros I approve myself. Above that it needs a second approver from the finance controller team.
What happens when that controller is away?
Then it sits. Last month two invoices from our biggest carrier waited about a week because Marc was on leave and nobody else had the rights.
We sometimes just email the CFO and ask her to approve from her phone, but she hates that.
Got it. And the approval limit, is that the same for every supplier?
I think so, I'd have to check the policy. Our carriers are mostly above the limit anyway.

mustInclude: Probes the gap between 'about a day' and the week-long waits, e.g. how often invoices exceed the limit or how often the controller is unavailable
Is a single question the user can ask now
mustNotInclude: Re-asks how long approvals take in general
checkpoints.ideal: Ask what share of invoices, by value, goes above five thousand euros and therefore depends on the controller, since carriers are mostly above the limit.

mustInclude: States that the approval limit per supplier is still unconfirmed (Dana must check the policy)
Names a concrete next question or follow-up
mustNotInclude: Treats the approval limit question as fully answered
Treats end-to-end approval time as settled at one day
checkpoints.ideal: The limit was only mentioned with uncertainty; ask Dana to confirm the policy, and note the conflict between 'a day' and week-long waits.
